'''''Hibiscus arnottianus''''' is a species of [[flowering plant]] in the mallow family [[Malvaceae]]. It is a shrub or small tree native to the islands of [[Oahu]] and [[Molokai]] in the [[Hawaiian Islands]],<ref name = powo/> where it grows in [[Hawaiian tropical rainforests|tropical rainforest]].<ref name = powo/><ref name = iucn/>

The species is threatened by competition with invasive non-native plants and by predation and habitat degradation by introduced animals. Invasive plants alter its native habitat and compete for space, light, moisture, and nutrients. feral pigs (''[[Sus domesticus]]''), goats (''[[Capra hircus]]''), and [[axis deer]] (''Axis axis'') damage plants and degrade the species' habitat by excessive browsing, trampling, and rooting for food. Introduced rats (''[[Rattus rattus]]'') and introduced slugs and snails feed on plant parts and fruits. The species is also threatened by landslides, fire, and drought, which are worsened by habitat degradation. The species is assessed as [[endangered species|endangered]] in the [[IUCN Red List]].<ref name = iucn/>

Three subspecies are accepted.<ref name = powo/>
*'''''Hibiscus arnottianus'' subsp. ''arnottianus''''' (synonym ''Hibiscus boryanus'' {{small|Hook. & Arn.}}) – native to the [[Waiʻanae Range]] of Oahu from 120 to 790 meters elevation.<ref name = iucn/> Subspecies ''arnottianus'' is assessed as endangered by the IUCN.<ref>{{cite iucn |author=Keir, M. |year=2020 |title=''Hibiscus arnottianus'' subsp. ''arnottianus'' |volume=2020 |article-number=e.T103802289A103802294 |doi=10.2305/IUCN.UK.2020-1.RLTS.T103802289A103802294.en |access-date=21 May 2025}}</ref>
*'''''Hibiscus arnottianus'' subsp. ''immaculatus''''' {{small|(M.J.Roe) D.M.Bates}} (synonym ''Hibiscus immaculatus'' {{small|M.J.Roe}}) – native to eastern Molokai, including the Waihanau and Papalaua valleys, from 300 to 800 meters elevation.<ref name = iucn/> Subspecies ''immaculatus'' is assessed as [[Critically-endangered species|critically endangered]] by the IUCN.<ref>{{cite iucn |author=Keir, M. |year=2020 |title=''Hibiscus arnottianus'' subsp. ''immaculatus'' |volume=2020 |article-number=e.T33624A78767227 |doi=10.2305/IUCN.UK.2020-1.RLTS.T33624A78767227.en |access-date=21 May 2025}}</ref>
*'''''Hibiscus arnottianus'' subsp. ''punaluuensis''''' {{small|(Skottsb.) D.M.Bates}} (synonym ''Hibiscus punaluuensis'' {{small|(Skottsb.) O.Deg. & I.Deg.}}) – native to the [[Koolau Range]] of eastern Oahu from 120 to 790 meters elevation.<ref name = iucn/> Subspecies ''punaluuensis'' is assessed as endangered by the IUCN.<ref>{{cite iucn |author=Keir, M. |year=2020 |title=''Hibiscus arnottianus'' subsp. ''punaluuensis'' |volume=2020 |article-number=e.T103802306A103821195 |doi=10.2305/IUCN.UK.2020-1.RLTS.T103802306A103821195.en |access-date=21 May 2025}}</ref>
